title: Dragon Head
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Returning from a school trip, Teru survives a train derailment in a tunnel during an earthquake with two classmates: bullied Nobuo, who descends into madness, and injured Ako. Escaping into an ash-covered Japan where society has collapsed and Mount Fuji has vanished, they meet unstable soldiers, survivors planning mass suicide and a scientist's cult using fear-suppressing drugs, and cling to hope amid ongoing disaster (Wikipedia; ANN Manga Guide; Tokyopop blurb via AniList).
life_message: Even when society and certainty collapse, people must face fear honestly and hold on to each other and to hope.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Teru must fight Nobuo and Nimura personally; no courts remain (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty narrows to Teru and Ako; Teru's family lost (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Authority figures (Nimura) shown unstable and untrustworthy (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Science cult and darkness worship both shown (Wikipedia; ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Bare survival is the whole story (AniList Survival 100%).

folkways.japan: Earthquake, volcano and a vanished Mount Fuji tap Japanese disaster anxieties, and the school-trip framing reflects Japanese school life.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers stress bleak mood and suspense, not a stated lesson.
delivery.note: Despair and cult answers to fear are shown through characters the heroes resist, without speeches noted in sources.

winners_losers: Teru and Ako survive and hold on to hope; Nobuo, Nimura and the cult represent failed responses to fear. Sympathy goes to endurance and care.
to_verify: ANN Manga Guide covers volume 1 only; later-volume content from Wikipedia plot
